checks.note: The article says that before Leiden, scholars 'used divergent conventions to indicate the condition of the text and editorial corrections or restorations'. The system was agreed at Leiden in 1931 and published in 1932, and it standardised the brackets. The bearing (an 1847 [ ] cannot be read by the modern convention) is a fair inference.

checks.correction: The general claim can be verified, but not from memory. The TLG Beta Code Manual says square brackets mark 'either editorial or conjectural additions to the text or deletions from the text', that they are 'Generally addition in papyrological and epigraphical use', and that they are 'Indeterminate between addition or deletion in codical use'. A. Mahoney, 'Epigraphy' (TEI Electronic Textual Editing, https://vault.tei-c.de/ETE/Preview/mahoney.html), notes that pre-1931 texts 'use similar, but different conventions' and that square brackets 'may denote additions rather than subtractions'. I could not verify the specific attribution of deletion-brackets to 'Bekker/Teubner practice', so cite these sources instead.
checks.note: Vincent 1847 itself shows how variable the practice was: he uses [ ] for supplements and ( ) for words to delete (see Q09-new-04 and -05).

§1122: the generic article denotes a class. §1126: 'The generic article is frequently omitted, especially with abstracts (1132), without appreciable difference in meaning'. §1131: 'Abstract substantives generally have the article'. §1132: names of virtues, vices, arts, sciences and occupations often omit it. The summary and bearing are fair.
The text reads 'οἷον δίτονον, τόνος, ἡμιτόνιον, διὰ τεσσάρων, διὰ πέντε, διὰ πασῶν καὶ τὰ ὅμοια'. Section 5, Jan p. 187.8-9 (pb 187 in the First1KGreek XML).
Bailly has 'δίεσις, εως (ἡ)'. Sense I.2 is musical: semitone or diesis (Philol.); chromatic diesis (Aristox. apud Ptol.); quarter-tone (A. Quint.). The noun is feminine, and the bearing is fair.
§1123: 'In the singular the generic article makes a single object the representative of the entire class'.

checks.correction: δίεσις does not occur in chapter 11 (Περὶ τοῦ δὶς διὰ πασῶν κατὰ τὸ διάτονον γένος, 11.1-11.6). The anarthrous δίεσις in a sequence of intervals is in chapter 12, on the enharmonic progression: 'τὸ δὲ ἐναρμόνιον τὴν προκοπὴν φυσικῶς τοιαύτην ἔχει· δίεσις, ὅπερ ἐστὶν ἡμιτονίου ἥμισυ, καὶ πάλιν ἄλλη δίεσις, … ὅλον δίτονον ἀσύνθετον'. A further anarthrous example is in chapter 9, in the Philolaus quotation: 'τρίʼ ἐπόγδοα καὶ δίεσις'.
checks.note: The bearing (bare δίεσις is acceptable) stands.

§1118: the article marks individuals or classes (the generic article). §1126: generic article 'frequently omitted, especially with abstracts … without appreciable difference in meaning'. §§1131-1132 as in Q09-03.

So the article goes with single contrasted subjects, not with every case where intervals are subjects.

summary:
All 26 findings checked. 15 are confirmed, 11 corrected, and none is wrong, not found or unopenable. Vincent 1847 was checked against archive.org page images (offsets differ by section: n397 = p. 374, n434 = p. 405, n33 = p. 14). The 1693 Veterum mathematicorum p. 315 was also checked from its page image. The other sources were checked as follows: First1KGreek XML for Cleonides and Theon, Jan's OCR, Smyth on Alpheios, Bailly, Wikipedia, and eulogikon for Nicomachus. Vincent's own pages on and around p. 340, his print of this text, were not opened.

Main corrections:
- Vincent does state one editorial sign, contrary to new-01: p. 482, n. 4 says round parentheses mark Pachymeres' additions to his Ptolemy quotations. No key exists for [ ], and the 'crochet' OCR search has two unrelated hits, not one.
- 'PAR UN [SECOND] ANONYME' is on p. 14 (n33), not p. 33 (new-17).
- The Nicomachus δίεσις is in chapter 12 (also 9), not 11 (Q09-07).
- In Cleonides, 'ἐλάχιστον μὲν τὸ διὰ τεσσάρων' is §8 (Jan p. 194), not §5 or §7 (new-14). In his §5 list 'ἐλάττω … δίεσις, ἡμιτόνιον…' the intervals are subjects yet have no article.
- The Aristotle De sensu quotation is in Jan's 'Aristotelis loci de musica', p. 21, not his prolegomena (new-15).
- p. 312 has a second note, 'Sous-ent. τόνοις', on δυσίν (new-09).
- The from-memory bracket claim is supported by the TLG Beta Code Manual and Mahoney instead (Q09-02).
- At p. 453 only ms. A omits [καὶ διέσεως], so those brackets mark a one-witness omission (new-07).

Overall, the Vincent evidence holds up. His square brackets regularly enclose supplements, often without a note, and round parentheses with 'Mot surabondant' mark words to delete. Downloads are in (local working folder)
